title: The verb in second place
description: Keep the Swedish verb in second place, and know when the subject moves behind it.

guide.summary: Swedish main clauses keep their verb in second place: whatever comes first, the verb follows it. Learn what fills first place, where the subject goes, and why subordinate clauses do not follow the rule.

sections.title: The verb is always second
sections.text: In a Swedish main clause, the verb that shows tense (äter, åt, vill, ska) is always the second element. An element can be one word or a phrase: jag, Anna, min mamma, på kvällen. Short adverbs such as ofta, alltid, aldrig and inte come after the verb, never between the subject and the verb as in English.
steps: Find the subject: who does it?
Put the tense-carrying verb straight after it.
Put ofta, alltid, aldrig or inte after the verb.
watch: English says I often drink; Swedish says jag dricker ofta, never jag ofta dricker.
Min mamma is one element: two words, but one place.

sections.title: Something else first: the subject moves behind the verb
sections.text: You can start a main clause with a time, a place or even the object. That element takes first place, the verb keeps second place, and the subject moves to third, right after the verb. Swedes start sentences this way all the time.
steps: Put the time, place or object first.
Put the verb next.
Put the subject straight after the verb.

examples.en: Today I am going to Stockholm.

watch: Idag jag åker is the most common mistake for English speakers: only one element may come before the verb.
Words like sedan, nu and igår count as first place too: Sedan dricker jag kaffe.

sections.title: Questions with a question word
sections.text: A question word (vad, var, när, hur, varför, vem) takes first place, so the verb comes second and the subject third. Swedish has no helper like English do or are: the main verb itself moves.
steps: Put the question word first.
Put the verb next.
Then the subject and the rest.
watch: Never add gör for English do: Vad äter du? not Vad gör du äter?
When the question word is itself the subject, nothing moves: Vem kommer?

sections.title: Yes or no questions start with the verb
sections.text: Without a question word, the question opens with the verb and the subject follows. Again, there is no helper: do you drink is simply dricker du.
steps: Take the statement.
Swap the subject and the verb.
End with a question mark.
watch: Gör du pratar svenska? is wrong: drop gör and start with pratar.

sections.title: Two verbs: only the first one counts
sections.text: With vill, kan, ska or måste plus another verb, only the first verb takes second place. The subject stays between the two verbs when it moves, and the infinitive comes after it, without att.
steps: Find the verb that shows tense: vill, kan, ska, måste.
Put it in second place.
If something else is first, put the subject right after that verb.
Put the infinitive after the subject.
watch: Not Nu vill äta jag: the subject goes between the two verbs.
Vill, kan, ska and måste take the infinitive without att.

sections.title: A när- or om-clause first
sections.text: A whole subordinate clause can stand in first place: När jag kommer hem, Om det regnar. It counts as one element, so the main verb comes straight after it, then the subject. A comma after the clause is common but not required.
steps: Treat the whole clause as first place.
Put the main verb right after it.
Then the subject.

examples.sv: När jag kommer hem, äter jag.
examples.en: When I get home, I eat.

examples.sv: Om du är hungrig, kan du äta nu.
examples.en: If you are hungry, you can eat now.

watch: English keeps I eat after the clause; Swedish says äter jag.
Inside the clause itself the order stays subject, verb: när jag kommer.

sections.title: Inside a subordinate clause: subject before verb
sections.text: After att (that), eftersom (because), när (when) and om (if), the clause does not follow the verb-second rule. The subject simply comes before the verb, as in English.
steps: Spot the link word: att, eftersom, när, om.
After it, put the subject.
Then the verb.

examples.sv: Jag tror att Erik är hemma.
examples.en: I think that Erik is at home.

examples.sv: Han säger att han kommer imorgon.
examples.en: He says that he is coming tomorrow.

watch: Do not invert after att: att jag äter, never att äter jag.

steps: Find the subject and put it first.
Put the tense-carrying verb second.
Put ofta, alltid or aldrig after the verb.
See what stands first: a time, a place or an object.
Put the verb straight after it.
Put the subject after the verb.
Put the question word first.
Put the verb second, with no gör.
Put the subject after the verb.
Start with the verb.
Put the subject next.
Never add gör as a helper.
Find the first verb: vill, kan, ska, måste.
Put it second.
If the subject moves, place it between the two verbs.
Treat the whole när- or om-clause as first place.
Put the main verb right after it.
Then the subject.
Spot att, eftersom, när or om.
Put the subject right after it.
Then the verb.

exercises.hint: In a Swedish main clause, what must stand in second place?
exercises.feedback: The subject Jag fills first place, so the verb takes second place at once.
exercises.explanation: Jag dricker ofta kaffe: the verb comes straight after the subject, and ofta follows the verb.

mistakes.why: That is the English order, I often drink. In Swedish, a word like often cannot squeeze in between the subject and the verb: the verb must take second place.

exercises.instruction: Write åker and alltid in the right order.
exercises.hint: Anna is first. What must come second?
exercises.feedback: The verb comes right after the subject; alltid waits behind it.
exercises.explanation: Anna åker alltid buss till jobbet: subject, verb, then the adverb alltid.

mistakes.why: This copies English, Anna always takes. Alltid pushes the verb to third place, and a Swedish main clause keeps its verb second.

exercises.source: We often eat dinner at home.
exercises.hint: Subject, then verb, then often.
exercises.feedback: Often follows the verb in a Swedish main clause.
exercises.explanation: Vi äter ofta middag hemma: vi is first, the verb äter second, and ofta comes after it.

mistakes.why: Often sits between the subject and the verb, as in English. That puts the verb third, which a Swedish main clause does not allow.

exercises.source: I always drink tea in the evening.
answers: Jag dricker alltid te på kvällen.
På kvällen dricker jag alltid te.
exercises.hint: Where does always go in Swedish: before or after the verb?
exercises.feedback: In a main clause the verb is second, so always comes after it.
exercises.explanation: Jag dricker alltid te på kvällen: jag first, the verb second, alltid after the verb.

answers: Jag alltid dricker te på kvällen.
mistakes.why: Always stands before the verb, as in English. Then the verb is third; in a Swedish main clause it has to be second.

answers: På kvällen jag dricker alltid te.
mistakes.why: Starting with på kvällen is fine, but then the verb must follow it directly, before the subject.

exercises.hint: Count the places: where is the verb now?
exercises.feedback: Aldrig has pushed the verb into third place.
exercises.explanation: Erik äter aldrig frukost: the verb takes second place and aldrig follows it.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. Aldrig stands between the subject and the verb, so the verb is third.
Now aldrig is first and the subject second, so the verb is still third. Whatever stands first, the verb comes next.

exercises.instruction: Add ofta (often) to the sentence. Write the whole sentence.

alternatives.message: Correct: with ofta first, the verb comes next and Sara follows it. Starting with the subject is the more neutral choice.
Correct too. The most usual place for ofta is right after the verb: Sara läser ofta tidningen.

exercises.hint: Ofta goes after the verb.
exercises.feedback: Keep Sara first and the verb second; slot ofta in behind the verb.
exercises.explanation: Sara läser ofta tidningen: the verb stays in second place and ofta follows it.

mistakes.why: Ofta has slipped in before the verb, which pushes the verb to third place.

exercises.hint: Idag already fills first place.
exercises.feedback: When a time word comes first, the verb follows it and the subject comes after the verb.
exercises.explanation: Idag åker jag till Stockholm: idag is first, so the verb åker is second and jag moves behind it.

mistakes.why: This is the English order, today I go. In Swedish idag takes first place, so the next word has to be the verb, not the subject.

exercises.hint: What is in first place here?
exercises.feedback: På kvällen is first, so the verb takes second place.
exercises.explanation: På kvällen tittar vi på tv: the time phrase is first, the verb second, the subject third.

mistakes.why: The subject is in second place and the verb third. After a time phrase, the verb must come before the subject.
The verb is in the right place, but the sentence has lost its subject. Swedish always needs one, here vi.

exercises.instruction: Write ringer and jag in the right order.
exercises.hint: Imorgon is in first place.
exercises.feedback: A time word first sends the subject behind the verb.
exercises.explanation: Imorgon ringer jag min mamma: imorgon first, the verb second, then jag.

mistakes.why: With imorgon first, the subject cannot take second place too. The verb comes next, and the subject follows it.

exercises.hint: Start with the time phrase, then count to two.
exercises.feedback: The verb follows the time phrase, then the subject.
exercises.explanation: På lördagar spelar vi fotboll: the whole phrase på lördagar counts as first place, so spelar is second.

mistakes.why: After på lördagar the subject came next, so the verb ended up third. The verb needs second place.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Swedish. Start with tomorrow.
exercises.source: Tomorrow we are eating at a restaurant.
answers: I morgon äter vi på restaurang.
Imorgon äter vi på en restaurang.
I morgon äter vi på en restaurang.
Imorgon ska vi äta på restaurang.
I morgon ska vi äta på restaurang.
Imorgon ska vi äta på en restaurang.
I morgon ska vi äta på en restaurang.
exercises.hint: Tomorrow first, then the verb.
exercises.feedback: Imorgon fills first place, so the verb goes second and vi third.
exercises.explanation: Imorgon äter vi på restaurang: time word, verb, subject.

answers: Imorgon vi äter på en restaurang.
mistakes.why: The subject came straight after imorgon, so the verb is third. With a time word first, the verb must come before the subject.

answers: Imorgon vi ska äta på restaurang.
mistakes.why: Ska can be used, but here too the order is off: after imorgon the verb comes next, then the subject.

exercises.hint: Sedan counts as first place.
exercises.feedback: After sedan the verb comes next, not the subject.
exercises.explanation: Sedan dricker jag kaffe: sedan first, verb second, subject third.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. Sedan is first and jag second, so the verb is in third place.
Now jag is first, but sedan still sits before the verb, which leaves the verb third.

exercises.instruction: Start the sentence with Igår. Write the whole sentence.
exercises.hint: When igår moves to the front, what must come next?
exercises.feedback: Igår takes first place, so the verb stays second and jag moves behind it.
exercises.explanation: Igår träffade jag Anna: the verb holds second place, and the subject moves to third.

mistakes.why: Igår moved to the front, but the subject still comes before the verb, so the verb is third.
The verb is second, but the subject and object have swapped places. The subject jag goes straight after the verb, and Anna, who was met, comes last.

exercises.instruction: Start the sentence with Den boken (that book). Write the whole sentence.
answers: Den boken läste jag i går.
exercises.hint: The object den boken now fills first place.
exercises.feedback: Even an object at the front counts as first place, so the verb comes next.
exercises.explanation: Den boken läste jag igår: object first, verb second, subject third. Starting with the object stresses it.

mistakes.why: The object went to the front, but the subject followed it, so the verb landed in third place.
Two things stand before the verb. Only one element may come before the verb in a main clause; igår stays at the end.

exercises.hint: The question word takes first place.
exercises.feedback: Var is first, so the verb comes second and the subject after it.
exercises.explanation: Var bor du? The question word fills first place, then verb, then subject.

mistakes.why: With var first, the subject cannot take second place. The verb must come straight after the question word.

exercises.instruction: Write äter and du in the right order.
exercises.hint: Vad is in first place.
exercises.feedback: After a question word, the verb comes next.
exercises.explanation: Vad äter du till frukost? Question word, verb, subject: the same verb-second rule as in a statement.

mistakes.why: The subject came before the verb, so the verb is third. After a question word, the verb goes second.

exercises.hint: Question word first, verb second.
exercises.feedback: Swedish has no do or are helper: the main verb itself moves before the subject.
exercises.explanation: Vad äter du idag? Vad first, äter second, du third.

mistakes.why: The subject stands before the verb, so the verb is third. After vad the verb comes next.
Swedish never uses gör as a helper like English do. The verb äter itself moves to second place.

exercises.hint: Varför first, then the verb.
exercises.feedback: The verb är goes right after varför.
exercises.explanation: Varför är du trött? Question word, verb, subject.

mistakes.why: The subject came before the verb. After a question word, the verb must take second place.

exercises.hint: Where should the verb be?
exercises.feedback: After hur, the verb comes before the subject.
exercises.explanation: Hur mår du? Hur is first, the verb mår second, du third.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. The subject sits in second place and pushes the verb to third.

exercises.instruction: Ask where Erik lives. Use var and write the whole question.
exercises.hint: Var replaces i Malmö and goes first.
exercises.feedback: The question word takes first place; then the verb, then the subject.
exercises.explanation: Var bor Erik? Var replaces the place and takes first position, so bor comes second and Erik third.

mistakes.why: The subject came straight after var, so the verb is third. After a question word, the verb goes second.
That is a yes or no question: is Erik living in Malmö? The task asks where he lives, so it needs the question word.
The question word already stands for the place, so i Malmö has to go.

exercises.instruction: Choose the start of the question: Do you drink coffee?
exercises.hint: A yes or no question has no question word. What goes first?
exercises.feedback: Swedish yes or no questions open with the verb.
exercises.explanation: Dricker du kaffe? The verb comes first and the subject follows. There is no helper like English do.

mistakes.why: That is statement order. Written with a question mark it can sound like surprise, but a normal yes or no question starts with the verb.
Swedish does not build questions with gör, the way English uses do. The main verb itself goes first.

exercises.instruction: Write är and du in the right order to ask: Are you at home today?
exercises.hint: No question word: the verb starts the question.
exercises.feedback: In a yes or no question the verb comes first.
exercises.explanation: Är du hemma idag? The verb opens the question and the subject follows.

mistakes.why: This is the order of a statement, you are at home today. To ask, the verb moves to the front.

exercises.hint: Which word do you not need?
exercises.feedback: The verb itself starts the question; there is no do.
exercises.explanation: Bor du i Stockholm? Verb first, then subject.

mistakes.why: Gör is not a question helper in Swedish. Leave it out and let the verb open the question.

exercises.hint: Start with the verb.
exercises.feedback: Does has no Swedish equivalent: the verb goes first.
exercises.explanation: Jobbar Anna idag? The verb opens the question and Anna follows.

mistakes.why: Swedish has no helper like does. The main verb itself moves to the front.
That is a statement with a question mark. A plain yes or no question starts with the verb.

exercises.hint: Which word is English thinking?
exercises.feedback: Gör is not a question helper in Swedish.
exercises.explanation: Pratar du svenska? Drop gör and let the verb open the question.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. Gör copies English do; Swedish does not use it to make questions.
Gör is gone, but this is now statement order with a question mark. The verb should come first.

exercises.instruction: Turn the statement into a yes or no question.
exercises.hint: Swap the subject and the verb.
exercises.feedback: In a yes or no question the verb comes first.
exercises.explanation: Kommer ni imorgon? The verb moves to the front and ni follows it.

mistakes.why: Only the punctuation changed. To ask, the verb has to move to the front.
Swedish does not add gör to ask a question; the verb itself moves to the front.

exercises.hint: Only the first verb, vill, counts for second place.
exercises.feedback: Nu is first, so vill must be second, and the subject comes after it.
exercises.explanation: Nu vill jag äta: vill holds second place; the infinitive äta stays further back.

mistakes.why: Nu already fills first place, so the subject cannot also stand before the verb. Vill must come straight after nu.

exercises.instruction: Write ska and jag in the right order.
exercises.hint: Which verb has to be second?
exercises.feedback: Ska is the verb that changes form, so it takes second place.
exercises.explanation: Imorgon ska jag jobba hemma: imorgon first, ska second, jag third, then jobba.

mistakes.why: The subject came before the verb after imorgon, so ska is third. The first verb must be in second place.

exercises.hint: After vill, is there a word for to?
exercises.feedback: Vill takes the second verb directly, with no att.
exercises.explanation: Jag vill äta nu: jag first, vill second, then äta. Modal verbs like vill, kan, ska and måste take the infinitive without att.

mistakes.why: Vill is followed by the plain infinitive, without att. Leave that tile unused.

exercises.hint: Nu first; which verb comes second?
exercises.feedback: The first verb takes second place; the infinitive goes at the end.
exercises.explanation: Nu vill jag äta: nu first, vill second, jag third, äta last.

mistakes.why: The subject came straight after nu, which pushes vill to third place.

exercises.instruction: Start the sentence with På lördag. Write the whole sentence.
exercises.source: Vi ska spela fotboll på lördag.
answers: På lördag ska vi spela fotboll.
exercises.hint: The first verb, ska, keeps second place.
exercises.feedback: På lördag goes first, ska second, vi third, spela after it.
exercises.explanation: På lördag ska vi spela fotboll: only the first verb moves before the subject; spela stays behind.

answers: På lördag vi ska spela fotboll.
mistakes.why: The subject came before ska, which puts the verb third.

answers: På lördag ska spela vi fotboll.
mistakes.why: Ska is rightly second, but the subject belongs between the two verbs, not after both.

answers: På lördag spela vi ska fotboll.
mistakes.why: The infinitive moved forward. It is the first verb, the one that shows tense, that takes second place.

exercises.source: På kvällen vi kan titta på film.
answers: På kvällen kan vi titta på film.
exercises.hint: Which verb should be second?
exercises.feedback: After the time phrase, kan comes next, then the subject.
exercises.explanation: På kvällen kan vi titta på film: time phrase first, kan second, vi third.

answers: På kvällen vi kan titta på film.
mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. The subject sits before kan, so the verb is third.

answers: På kvällen titta vi kan på film.
mistakes.why: The wrong verb moved. Kan is the verb that carries the tense, and it is kan that takes second place.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Swedish. Start with tomorrow.
exercises.hint: Tomorrow, then måste, then the subject.
exercises.feedback: Måste is the first verb, so it takes second place.
exercises.explanation: Imorgon måste jag jobba: time word, måste, jag, then the infinitive.

mistakes.why: The subject came before måste, which leaves the verb third.
Måste is rightly second, but the subject must come straight after it, before the second verb.

exercises.hint: The whole när-clause counts as first place.
exercises.feedback: After a clause at the front, the main verb comes next.
exercises.explanation: När jag kommer hem, äter jag middag: the när-clause is first place, so äter is second and jag third.

mistakes.why: The när-clause already fills first place, so the subject cannot come next. The verb must follow the clause directly.

exercises.instruction: Write stannar and vi in the right order.
exercises.hint: Om det regnar is one block in first place.
exercises.feedback: After the om-clause, the verb comes before the subject.
exercises.explanation: Om det regnar, stannar vi hemma: the whole om-clause is first, the verb second.

mistakes.why: The om-clause counts as first place, so the subject cannot stand in second. The verb comes straight after the clause.

exercises.source: When I am tired, I sleep.
answers: När jag är trött, sover jag.
exercises.hint: The när-clause is one block. What comes after it?
exercises.feedback: After the clause, the verb comes first, then the subject.
exercises.explanation: När jag är trött, sover jag: the clause is first place, sover is second.

answers: När jag är trött, jag sover.
mistakes.why: After the clause, the subject came first, so the main verb is in third place.

exercises.instruction: Start the sentence with the när-clause. Write the whole sentence.
exercises.source: Jag äter när jag kommer hem.
answers: När jag kommer hem, äter jag.
exercises.hint: Move the när-clause to the front. What follows it?
exercises.feedback: The clause now fills first place, so the main verb comes right after it.
exercises.explanation: När jag kommer hem, äter jag: the clause is first, äter second, jag third. Inside the clause, jag still comes before kommer.

answers: När jag kommer hem, jag äter.
mistakes.why: The subject follows the clause, so the main verb is third. After a clause at the front, the verb comes next.

answers: När kommer jag hem, äter jag.
mistakes.why: The main clause is right, but the order inside the när-clause changed. A subordinate clause keeps subject before verb.

exercises.source: Om du är hungrig, du kan äta nu.
answers: Om du är hungrig, kan du äta nu.
exercises.hint: The om-clause is first place. What must follow it?
exercises.feedback: Kan must come right after the clause.
exercises.explanation: Om du är hungrig, kan du äta nu: om-clause first, kan second, du third.

answers: Om du är hungrig, du kan äta nu.
mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. The subject comes straight after the clause, so kan is third.

answers: Om är du hungrig, kan du äta nu.
mistakes.why: The main clause is fixed, but now the om-clause has the verb before its subject. Inside a subordinate clause, the subject comes first.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Swedish. Start with when.
exercises.source: When it rains, we stay at home.
answers: När det regnar, stannar vi hemma.
exercises.hint: När-clause first, then the verb.
exercises.feedback: After the när-clause, stannar comes before vi.
exercises.explanation: När det regnar, stannar vi hemma: the clause fills first place, so the verb is second.

answers: När det regnar, vi stannar hemma.
mistakes.why: After the när-clause the subject came first, putting the verb in third place.

answers: När regnar det, stannar vi hemma.
mistakes.why: Inside the när-clause, the subject det must come before the verb.

exercises.hint: Inside an att-clause, which comes first: subject or verb?
exercises.feedback: A subordinate clause keeps the subject before the verb.
exercises.explanation: Hon säger att hon är trött: after att, subject then verb, with no inversion.

mistakes.why: Verb before subject belongs in questions and after a fronted word in a main clause. After att, the subject comes first.

exercises.instruction: Write bor and du in the right order.
exercises.hint: Att starts a subordinate clause.
exercises.feedback: Inside an att-clause, the subject goes before the verb.
exercises.explanation: Jag vet att du bor i Malmö: subject du, then the verb bor.

mistakes.why: That is question order. After att the clause keeps the subject first.

exercises.source: I think that Erik is at home.
answers: Jag tror att Erik är hemma.
exercises.hint: After att: subject, then verb.
exercises.feedback: The att-clause keeps the subject before the verb.
exercises.explanation: Jag tror att Erik är hemma: Erik comes before är inside the att-clause.

answers: Jag tror att är Erik hemma.
mistakes.why: The verb came before the subject inside the att-clause. Only main clauses invert; after att, the subject comes first.

exercises.source: I am eating now because I am hungry.
answers: Jag äter nu eftersom jag är hungrig.
exercises.hint: Eftersom starts a subordinate clause.
exercises.feedback: After eftersom, the subject comes before the verb.
exercises.explanation: Jag äter nu eftersom jag är hungrig: inside the eftersom-clause, jag comes before är.

answers: Jag äter nu eftersom är jag hungrig.
mistakes.why: The verb came before the subject inside the eftersom-clause. A subordinate clause keeps the subject first.

exercises.source: Han säger att kommer han imorgon.
answers: Han säger att han kommer imorgon.
Han säger att han kommer i morgon.
exercises.hint: Look at the att-clause.
exercises.feedback: After att, the subject comes first.
exercises.explanation: Han säger att han kommer imorgon: inside the att-clause, han comes before kommer.

answers: Han säger att kommer han imorgon.
mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. The att-clause has the verb before its subject, as if it were a question.

answers: Säger han att han kommer imorgon?
mistakes.why: The att-clause is fixed, but the main clause has become a question. Only the order after att needed changing.

exercises.instruction: Join the two sentences with att. Write one sentence.
answers: Jag vet att bussen kommer snart.
exercises.hint: Att introduces the second part.
exercises.feedback: After att, keep the subject before the verb.
exercises.explanation: Jag vet att bussen kommer snart: the att-clause keeps bussen before kommer.

answers: Jag vet att kommer bussen snart.
mistakes.why: The verb jumped before the subject inside the att-clause. Only main clauses do that.
The order is right, but the task asks you to join the sentences with att.

exercises.source: I know that you speak Swedish.
answers: Jag vet att du pratar svenska.
Jag vet att du talar svenska.
exercises.hint: Inside the att-clause: subject, then verb.
exercises.feedback: After att, du comes before the verb.
exercises.explanation: Jag vet att du pratar svenska: the att-clause keeps the subject first.

answers: Jag vet att pratar du svenska.
Jag vet att talar du svenska.
mistakes.why: The verb came before du inside the att-clause. That is question order, not used after att.
